body:
Tried a normal full table scan and works as expected
```
yugabyte=# explain (analyze, dist) select * from test;
                                                        QUERY PLAN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Seq Scan on test  (cost=10000000000.00..10000000100.00 rows=1000 width=8) (actual time=24.173..45.292 rows=1000 loops=1)
   Storage Table Read Requests: 2
   Storage Table Execution Time: 44.004 ms
 Planning Time: 0.094 ms
 Execution Time: 45.721 ms
 Storage Read Requests: 2
 Storage Write Requests: 0
 Storage Execution Time: 44.004 ms
 Peak Memory Usage: 0 kB
(9 rows)
```
The problem might be on the pushdown part.

Even for a simple scan, it won't return the rows
```
yugabyte=# explain analyze select from test;
                                                         QUERY PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Index Only Scan using test_pkey on test  (cost=0.00..114.00 rows=1000 width=0) (actual time=37.550..37.550 rows=0 loops=1)
   Heap Fetches: 0
 Planning Time: 0.096 ms
 Execution Time: 37.628 ms
 Peak Memory Usage: 0 kB
(5 rows)

yugabyte=# show enable_seqscan;
 enable_seqscan
----------------
 off
(1 row)

yugabyte=# select from test;
--
(0 rows)

yugabyte=# set enable_seqscan = on;
SET
yugabyte=# select from test;
--
(1000 rows)
```

Compared to PG
```
postgres=# show enable_seqscan ;
 enable_seqscan
----------------
 on
(1 row)

postgres=# create table test(k int primary key, v int);
CREATE TABLE
postgres=# insert into test select i, i from generate_series(1,1000) as i;
INSERT 0 1000
postgres=# select from test;
--
(1000 rows)

postgres=# set enable_seqscan = off;
SET
postgres=# select from test;
--
(1000 rows)
```
This confirms the output from YSQL is not correct but it seems not related to expressions (whether pushed down or not).

The problem is not related to the config enable_seqscan itself. Forcing an indexonlyscan generates the same problem:
```
yugabyte=# show enable_seqscan;
 enable_seqscan
----------------
 on
(1 row)

yugabyte=# explain analyze /*+ IndexOnlyScan(test) */ select from test;
                                                         QUERY PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Index Only Scan using test_pkey on test  (cost=0.00..114.00 rows=1000 width=0) (actual time=29.116..29.116 rows=0 loops=1)
 Planning Time: 0.370 ms
 Execution Time: 29.265 ms
 Peak Memory Usage: 0 kB
(4 rows)

yugabyte=# explain analyze /*+ IndexScan(test) */ select from test;
                                                         QUERY PLAN
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 YB Seq Scan on test  (cost=10000000000.00..10000000100.00 rows=1000 width=0) (actual time=12.432..20.375 rows=1000 loops=1)
 Planning Time: 0.258 ms
 Execution Time: 20.534 ms
 Peak Memory Usage: 0 kB
(4 rows)
```
While IndexScan doesn't have such problem.

Found 0 column refs in the requests. This is probably the cause. 

```
I0331 13:10:39.010843 3689110336 pg_session.cc:246] Applying operation: { READ active: 1 read_time: { read: <invalid> local_limit: <invalid> global_limit: <invalid> in_txn_limit: <invalid> serial_no: 0 } request: client: YQL_CLIENT_PGSQL stmt_id: 4453941536 schema_version: 0 hash_code: 32767 column_refs { } is_forward_scan: 1 is_aggregate: 0 limit: 1024 paging_state { next_partition_key: "7FFF" total_num_rows_read: 502 } return_paging_state: 1 table_id: "000033f1000030008000000000004000" partition_key: "7FFF" }
```
With storage rows impl (WIP), I can confirm that DocDB scans the expected number of rows
```
yugabyte=# explain (analyze, dist) /*+ IndexOnlyScan(test) */ select from test;
                                                         QUERY PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Index Only Scan using test_pkey on test  (cost=0.00..114.00 rows=1000 width=0) (actual time=18.944..18.944 rows=0 loops=1)
   Storage Index Rows Read: 1000
   Storage Index Read Requests: 2
   Storage Index Execution Time: 16.439 ms
 Planning Time: 0.294 ms
 Storage Rows Read: 1000
 Storage Read Requests: 2
 Storage Write Requests: 0
 Storage Execution Time: 16.439 ms
 Execution Time: 19.080 ms
 Peak Memory Usage: 0 kB
(11 rows)
```

After adding a secondary index on column v, the request includes one column ref and it returns expected results:
```
yugabyte=# explain (analyze, dist) /*+ IndexOnlyScan(test) */ select count(1) from test ;
                                                            QUERY PLAN
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Aggregate  (cost=116.50..116.51 rows=1 width=8) (actual time=20.365..20.366 rows=1 loops=1)
   ->  Index Only Scan using test_v on test  (cost=0.00..114.00 rows=1000 width=0) (actual time=19.007..20.014 rows=1000 loops=1)
         Storage Index Rows Read: 1000
         Storage Index Read Requests: 1
         Storage Index Execution Time: 17.331 ms
 Planning Time: 0.351 ms
 Storage Rows Read: 1000
 Storage Read Requests: 1
 Storage Write Requests: 0
 Storage Execution Time: 17.331 ms
 Execution Time: 20.557 ms
 Peak Memory Usage: 8 kB
(12 rows)

I0331 14:03:38.271780 3689110336 pg_session.cc:246] Applying operation: { READ active: 1 read_time: { read: <invalid> local_limit: <invalid> global_limit: <invalid> in_txn_limit: <invalid> serial_no: 0 } request: client: YQL_CLIENT_PGSQL stmt_id: 4510597408 schema_version: 0 targets { column_id: 10 } column_refs { ids: 10 } is_forward_scan: 1 is_aggregate: 0 limit: 1024 return_paging_state: 1 ysql_catalog_version: 4 table_id: "000033f1000030008000000000004100" col_refs { column_id: 10 attno: 1 } }
```
After dropping the index, the request then doesn't include any column refs and returns the bad results.
So this almost confirms the problem is that the request doesn't include column refs or not.
~When there is not column ref in the doc_db request, the returned is_nulls are true, while when col refs exist, the is_nulls are false. This is why PG layer stops and regards it to be empty results.~

The problem can also happen in IndexOnlyScan on non-primary index:
```
yugabyte=# explain (analyze, dist) /*+ IndexOnlyScan(test t_vi) */ select from test ;
                                                      QUERY PLAN
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
 Index Only Scan using t_vi on test  (cost=0.00..114.00 rows=1000 width=0) (actual time=17.704..17.704 rows=0 loops=1)
   Storage Index Rows Read: 1000
   Storage Index Read Requests: 1
   Storage Index Execution Time: 15.438 ms
 Planning Time: 0.336 ms
 Storage Rows Read: 1000
 Storage Read Requests: 1
 Storage Write Requests: 0
 Storage Execution Time: 15.438 ms
 Execution Time: 17.863 ms
 Peak Memory Usage: 0 kB
(11 rows)

```

issue.title: [YSQL] Remove placeholder targets when no targets specified in the statement

repository.name: yugabyte-db
repository.description: YugabyteDB - the cloud native distributed SQL database for mission-critical applications.

issue.body:
Jira Link: [DB-6088](https://yugabyte.atlassian.net/browse/DB-6088)
### Description

In case of no targets specified in a statement, like `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM <table>`, we need to insert a placeholder target in the DocDB request so that the pg_dml fetcher can properly recognize empty rows in the response. Otherwise, the pg_dml fetcher will stop early and return nothing to PG layer. As a result, PG won't count the rows correctly.

A better proper fix can be to make the pg_dml fetcher have knowledge of the specified targets and not stop iterating the rows too early.

The current places where it uses placeholder target includes YbForerignScan and IndexOnlyScans.

Related issue: 
1. Added placeholder for IndexOnlyScan: #16583
